content.text: The Interventional Radiologist at the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH) took the lead by placing the first ever Vena Caval Filter, which is a highly specialized procedure for the first time in Pakistan. AKUH is one of the leading hospitals providing opportunities for higher training, developing skills and creating environment for such sophisticated procedures.

Patients who have surgeries or long term bed confinement are prone to develop clotting in their leg veins. These clots can move into circulation and get impacted in the lung's major vessels. If a clot is large, it can cause sudden death. These clots when lodged into the lung vessels are removed by a major surgery.

A more sophisticated procedure for prevention of clots from reaching the lungs is to place a filter into a major vein, which connects the leg veins to the lungs and prevents any life- threatening pulmonary embolism. The procedure was done in the Radiology Department by a interventional radiologist under local anesthesia. The procedure takes 15 minutes to 1 hour without any risk to the patient.
